body:
N-13 DESIGN NOTE (drawing PR; the code PR follows once this is merged).

DRAWN (S-12, S-18, S-19, C and X): a song the server already knows it cannot get is grey with "Not available on your server" in place of the artist line (the grammar of "Not downloaded"); a Top result like that is a grey card with a quiet circle instead of Play. It keeps its place in the ranking (marked, never hidden). A tap does not try: nothing spins, the server is not asked, a snackbar gives the server's own sentence for the reason (+ "Try again in a few days." for not found). Play/Shuffle of a list leave such songs out. Offline wins (verdict not asked or shown, the row says only "Not downloaded"). Grey = the server already knew; S-17's red stays for a failure that may pass (I recommend a permanent refusal goes straight to grey: owner/lead to confirm).

WHAT THE SERVER REMEMBERS: columns on song_ref (precedent: cover_tried_at; migration 0012 or the next free number): missing_reason (not_found | removed | age_restricted), missing_at (first), missing_tried_at (last), missing_rev (the matcher's revision: a better matcher voids old verdicts at once, no sweep). RETRY WINDOW: 7 days from the last try. Inside it the verdict is true; after it nothing is shown and the next person's tap searches for real (one search), which starts a new window or clears it. Never a background sweep (the 10 look-ups rule).

ONE HOOK: YoutubeSource._candidates, beside remember_video. Empty search -> remember; inside the window -> raise not_found with NO search. That serves play, prepare, keep and import at once, so the 9 s and the repeat look-up go even before the app marks anything. Cleared in attach_file and remember_video; refmerge never lets a survivor with a file inherit a mark.

PERMANENT vs TEMPORARY (and a defect in built code): permanent = a search that ANSWERED with no acceptable candidate, or every candidate gone/age-gated. Never marked: YouTube blocked or resting, timeout, network, failed, too_big. A stored videoId that is gone must first fall back to one search (today it fails at once as "removed"); only a search with no answer marks. BUT today LeanResolver.resolve_ranked turns a FAILED search (timeout, service down) into DownloadError("unavailable"), which the route answers as 404 song_unavailable, reason "removed", retryable:false. So song_unavailable is NOT permanent today: a search outage already tells the app (PR #4) never to retry, and would mark every tapped song. Code PR step 1: a distinct code (search_failed -> 502 source_unreachable, retryable) with a test; only then the verdict.

HOW THE APP LEARNS: (a) a field on row_to_ref, unavailable: {reason, retryAfter} or null: reaches resolve, the tap path, playlist and library rows; marking and clearing also touch the files feed (today no feed carries a ref with no file and no like/entry, so a phone would never hear). (b) Search rows are Deezer songs with no ref, so (a) never reaches them: ONE batched read-only call per list, POST /refs/unavailable {songs: [described as resolve does]} -> verdicts in order, using refs.find (creates no ref, asks YouTube nothing), sent after the rows draw, not offline, not on a plain music server, cached until retryAfter. I recommend both.

CODE PR TESTS: search outage is not marked; no match is marked and the second tap makes 0 look-ups; window expiry; matcher revision; cleared by a file; merge; the batch call creates no ref; app greys, taps and skips. No goldens expected.
